SubTotal.description: Total of invoice excluding taxes. Calculated automatically by Xero from the invoice's line items. Only for ACCPAY and ACCREC invoices, where this opt-in capability is enabled for your organisation, can SubTotal be supplied on write – on a SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED invoice supplied together with TotalTax and Total, it is validated against the calculated line item totals (see RoundingAmount); it is ignored in all other cases. This write behaviour, and the returned value reflecting it, only applies to the Create and Update endpoints (POST/PUT) and to retrieving a single invoice by ID (GET by ID) – it does not apply when listing invoices (GET)

TotalTax.description: Total tax on invoice. Calculated automatically by Xero from the invoice's line items. Only for ACCPAY and ACCREC invoices, where this opt-in capability is enabled for your organisation, can TotalTax be supplied on write – on a SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED invoice supplied together with SubTotal and Total, it is validated against the calculated line item totals (see RoundingAmount); it is ignored in all other cases. This write behaviour, and the returned value reflecting it, only applies to the Create and Update endpoints (POST/PUT) and to retrieving a single invoice by ID (GET by ID) – it does not apply when listing invoices (GET)

Total.description: Total of Invoice tax inclusive (i.e. SubTotal + TotalTax + RoundingAmount). Calculated automatically by Xero from the invoice's line items. Only for ACCPAY and ACCREC invoices, where this opt-in capability is enabled for your organisation, can Total be supplied on write – on a SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED invoice supplied together with SubTotal and TotalTax, it is validated against the calculated line item totals plus RoundingAmount; in all other cases this will be ignored if it does not equal the sum of the LineAmounts. This write behaviour, and the returned value reflecting it, only applies to the Create and Update endpoints (POST/PUT) and to retrieving a single invoice by ID (GET by ID) – it does not apply when listing invoices (GET)

TotalDiscount.description: Total of discounts applied on the invoice line items

RoundingAmount.description: An optional rounding adjustment added to SubTotal + TotalTax to give Total (i.e. Total = SubTotal + TotalTax + RoundingAmount). Only applies to ACCPAY and ACCREC invoices, and only if this opt-in capability has been enabled for your organisation. Not validated while the invoice is DRAFT. For SUBMITTED and AUTHORISED invoices, RoundingAmount is only applied when SubTotal, TotalTax and Total are all supplied together, and must be between -0.10 and 0.10 – values outside this range are rejected with a validation error (on DRAFT invoices, an out-of-range value is ignored instead). This field is only settable and only returned via the Create and Update endpoints (POST/PUT) and when retrieving a single invoice by ID (GET by ID) – it is not returned when listing invoices (GET)

EnteredTotal.description: The total amount as originally entered for the invoice, before any RoundingAmount adjustment is applied. Only applies to ACCPAY and ACCREC invoices, and only if this opt-in capability has been enabled for your organisation. Can only be set while the invoice is DRAFT; once the invoice is no longer DRAFT this reflects Total. This field is only settable and only returned via the Create and Update endpoints (POST/PUT) and when retrieving a single invoice by ID (GET by ID) – it is not returned when listing invoices (GET)

Returns one Feed Connection, as a bare object rather than inside an envelope.

The response is `404 bank-feed-not-found` when the identifier names no Feed Connection, when
it names one belonging to a different Application, when it is an all-zeros GUID, and when it

operations.summary: Connect feeds to Xero Bank Accounts that already exist
operations.description:
Creates Feed Connections against Xero Bank Accounts the Organisation already has. Each
item must include the `accountId` of the account it connects to. Xero performs no matching of
its own, and `accountNumber` and `accountName` are ignored if supplied.

Use this endpoint whenever the customer has chosen an account, including when they are
reconnecting a feed that was previously terminated.

Each item is processed independently, and the response has one result per request item in
request order.

200.description:
All items are 2xx: each one reached its desired state, and there is nothing left for you
to do. A created item has `status` `SUCCESS` and `statusCode` `201`.

A response that mixes successful items with rejected or partially failed ones is a
`207`, not a `200`.

207.description:
Some items did not reach their desired state. Each item has its own result, so read
the `items` array rather than the envelope.

Partial failures are rare, and nearly all are recoverable by your app. On this endpoint a partial failure is `partial-failure-previous-connection-deletion` or `partial-failure-connection-creation`: resend the same item. `error.accountId` and `error.connectionId` identify the account and connection; `error.subtype` is optional diagnostics. If the resend returns 409 `feed-already-connected-in-current-organisation`, the earlier attempt was recorded: treat the item as created. A connection an earlier attempt left in Xero without a feed connection never causes that 409: the resend replaces it. See https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/bankfeeds/feedconnections-2-0-errors/#partial-failures .

`207` means the item codes were neither all 2xx nor all 4xx. A `PARTIAL_FAILURE` item has `statusCode` `500`: the item did not complete, and the state it left behind needs attention or could not be confirmed. `error.subtype` says which. A `REJECTED` item whose error is `internal-error` or `too-many-requests` also has `statusCode` `500`, so it makes the response a `207` (as does a batch in which all items are like that): something unexpected went wrong for that item, and nothing was written, or Xero confirmed that nothing took effect, so resend that item as it is.

operations.summary: Create Xero Bank Accounts and connect feeds to them
operations.description:
Creates a new Xero Bank Account for each item and connects a feed to it.

`accountId` must not be supplied. An item that includes one — including an all-zeros GUID, or a
value that is not a GUID at all — is rejected, because supplying an account identifier means
the Application intends to connect an account that already exists, which is what
`/FeedConnections/ExistingAccount` is for.

`accountNumber` and `accountName` are required here, since they describe the account being
created. If the Organisation already has an account with the requested name, the item is
rejected with `account-name-already-exists` naming that account, and no account is created.
The same applies to a second item in the same request that uses a name an earlier item
has just taken.

With `partial-failure-new-account-existence-not-confirmed` the account may or may not have been created, and nothing else was set up for it. The error has `error.accountName`, but no `error.accountId` or `error.connectionId`. Use the Accounting API to check whether an account named `error.accountName` exists. If it does, connect it through ExistingAccount. If it does not, resend the item. If your app has a user, you can show them this message instead: "Something went wrong. Please check whether your chosen account name now exists. If it does, connect it. If not, try creating the new one again." `error.subtype` is optional diagnostics. See https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/bankfeeds/feedconnections-2-0-errors/#partial-failures .

operations.summary: Terminate Feed Connections
operations.description:
Terminates the Feed Connections named in the request. Terminating a Feed Connection
discontinues the bank feed, and does not otherwise affect the customer's data in Xero.

Each item is identified by the Feed Connection `id` alone. An item naming a Feed Connection
that does not exist, has already been terminated, or belongs to a different Application is
reported as `feed-not-found-or-already-deleted` with `status` `SUCCESS` and `statusCode`
`204` — there was nothing to terminate, which is not a failure, and is reported the same way
a real termination is.

The same identifier may not appear twice in one request.

Re-sending a completed delete is idempotent. If an item reports `PARTIAL_FAILURE`, or
the original response was lost, resend the same DeleteRequests item. The retry
checks whether the connection remains and terminates it if needed. A `SUCCESS` item on the resend
means the deletion is complete, including `feed-not-found-or-already-deleted` at `statusCode` `204`.
If a retry keeps reporting `PARTIAL_FAILURE`, contact Xero support with the connection
id in `error.connectionId`.

200.description:
All items are 2xx: each one reached its desired state, and there is nothing left for you
to do. This includes a request in which none of the identifiers matched a connection to terminate,
since `feed-not-found-or-already-deleted` is reported at `statusCode` `204` — the
requested final state already holds, which is not a failure.

A response that mixes these with rejected or partially failed items is a `207`.

207.description:
Some items did not reach their desired state. Each item has its own result, so read
the `items` array rather than the envelope.

Partial failures are rare, and nearly all are recoverable by your app. On this endpoint only `partial-failure-connection-deletion` applies: resend the same DeleteRequests item. It checks whether the connection remains and terminates it if needed. A `SUCCESS` item on the resend means the deletion is complete, including `feed-not-found-or-already-deleted` at `statusCode` `204`, which means the earlier attempt had already finished it. `error.subtype` is optional diagnostics. If it keeps reporting `PARTIAL_FAILURE`, contact Xero support with the connection id from `error.connectionId`. See https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/bankfeeds/feedconnections-2-0-errors/#partial-failures .

`207` means the item codes were neither all 2xx nor all 4xx. A `PARTIAL_FAILURE` item has `statusCode` `500`: the item did not complete, and the state it left behind needs attention or could not be confirmed. `error.subtype` says which. A `REJECTED` item whose error is `internal-error` or `too-many-requests` also has `statusCode` `500`, so it makes the response a `207`: something unexpected went wrong for that item before anything was deleted, so resending the item is safe. The outcome for a single request item.

Read `status` rather than inferring the outcome from the presence of `error`. On a
termination an item can have both `SUCCESS` and an `error`, when the identifier did not
match a connection to terminate.

Read `statusCode` per item as well, rather than deriving it from the envelope: it is the
number the envelope itself is computed from. A `statusCode` of `204` is an idempotent
no-op, not a failure; one of `500` on a `partial-failure-*` type is not a server fault to
retry blindly. The item's `error` does not repeat the number as `status`.

rejected, since nothing was created.

status.description:
`SUCCESS` means the item reached the state the request asked for — on a create the
connection exists, on a termination it is gone, including the idempotent case where it
was already gone. `REJECTED` means nothing was written, or Xero confirmed that nothing took effect.
A `4xx` item needs correcting before it is sent again, and a `500` item can be resent as it is. `error` says why.
`PARTIAL_FAILURE` means the item did not complete, and the state it left behind needs
attention or could not be confirmed. `error.subtype` says which, `error.detail`
describes it, and the item needs attention that neither of the other two values
implies.

A client deserialising this into a closed set of `SUCCESS` and `REJECTED` will fail on
`PARTIAL_FAILURE`. That is intended rather than an oversight: binding it silently to
either of the other two would hide state that the partner has to act on.

statusCode.description:
The numeric status of this item: `201` on a created connection,
`204` on a terminated or already-absent one, a 4xx on a rejection, `500` on a partial
failure or on a rejection whose error is `internal-error` or `too-many-requests`. The response envelope is computed from the items' `statusCode` values: all 2xx is `200`,
all 4xx is `400`, anything else is `207`. So a partner can
size up one item without reading `status` and `error` together. Never `202` and
never `207`: those are envelope-only, and an item-level `207` would be numerically
inside 2xx, so a batch of partial failures could be reported as `200`.

parameters.name: balanceDate
parameters.description:
date, yyyy-MM-dd 

If no parameter is provided, the current date will be used.

The ‘balance date’ will return transactions based on the accounting date entered by the user.  Transactions before the balanceDate will be included.
The user has discretion as to which accounting period the transaction relates to.

The ‘balance date’  will control the latest maximum date of transactions included in the aggregate numbers.  Balance date does not affect the CurrentStatement object, as this will always return the most recent statement before asAtSystemDate (if specified)

parameters.name: asAtSystemDate
parameters.description:
date, yyyy-MM-dd 

If no parameter is provided, the current date will be used.

The ‘as at’ date will return transactions based on the  creation date.  It reflects the date the transactions were entered into Xero, not the accounting date.
The ‘as at’ date can not be overridden by the user.  This can be used to estimate a ‘historical frequency of reconciliation’.

The ‘as at’ date will affect the current statement in the response, as any candidate statements created after this date will be filtered out.  Thus the current statement returned will be the most recent statement prior to the specified ‘as at’ date.  Be aware that neither the begin date, nor the balance date, will affect the current statement.

Note;  information is only presented when system architecture allows, meaning historical cash validation information will be an estimate. In addition, delete events are not aware of the ‘as at’ functionality in this endpoint, meaning that transactions deleted at the time the API is accessed will be considered to always have been deleted.

date, yyyy-MM-dd

operations.summary: Get the balance of each general ledger account as at a given date
operations.description:
Retrieves account balances as at `date`, optionally including balances for one or
more prior comparison periods, and optionally filtered by account class, type,
account IDs, system account code, or tracking item.

### Filtering

- Filter by `class`, `type`, `accountIds`, and/or `systemAccountCodes`. These can be
  combined freely — when more than one is supplied, the server returns only accounts
  that match **all** of the supplied filters (an intersection, not a union).
- `type` values are matched case-sensitively, so use uppercase (for example `BANK`). Inventory
  asset accounts are reported as, and can only be filtered by, `INVENTORY`; filtering by
  their underlying account type does not match them.
- `trackingItemIds` and `unassignedToTrackingCategoryIds` can be used independently of
  the filters above to further narrow which accounts are returned.

### Comparison periods

- Supplying `comparisonPeriodCount` together with `comparisonPeriodSize` returns
  additional balances at prior points in time, in addition to the balance at `date`.
- The n-th comparison date is `date` shifted back n times `comparisonPeriodSize`. For `MONTH`,
  `QUARTER`, and `YEAR` sizes, a `date` that falls on the last day of its month keeps landing
  on the last day of the shifted month (so comparisons across February behave correctly).
- `comparisonPeriodCount` and `comparisonPeriodSize` must be supplied together.

### Bank accounts

Bank account data is only available to users with bank account view permission for the
organisation.

- If the request would include bank accounts and the user lacks this permission, it is
  rejected with `403 Forbidden`. A request is treated as including bank accounts when it
  has no account filters, filters by all five `class` values and nothing else, includes
  `BANK` in `type`, or lists a bank account in `accountIds`.
- For other requests (for example `class=ASSET`), bank accounts are silently excluded from
  the response for users without this permission, instead of the request being rejected.

### Results

Only accounts with a non-zero balance at a given date are returned; accounts and comparison
dates with a net-zero balance are omitted, so the response can be empty.

### Pagination

This endpoint does not paginate — all matching account balances are returned in a single
response.

parameters.description: Accounting basis for the balance calculation.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The date to calculate account balances as at, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

parameters.name: comparisonPeriodCount
parameters.description:
Number of additional comparison balances to return, each one further back in
time than the last. Must be supplied together with `comparisonPeriodSize`.

- **Minimum**: 1
- **Maximum**: 100

parameters.name: comparisonPeriodSize
parameters.description:
The unit of time each comparison period steps back by. Must be supplied
together with `comparisonPeriodCount`.

parameters.name: accountIds
parameters.description:
Filter to specific account IDs (GUIDs). Repeat the parameter for multiple
accounts.

- **Maximum**: 50 account IDs
- **Validation**: Returns 404 if any ID does not exist for the organisation

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Account classes to filter by. Can be combined with other filters.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
Account types to filter by (e.g. `BANK`, `CURRENT`, etc). Use `INVENTORY` to
match inventory asset accounts, regardless of their underlying account type.
Can be combined with other filters.

System account codes to filter by (e.g. `RETAINEDEARNINGS`,

200.description: Success - returns account balances as at `date`.

operations.summary: Get the net movement of each general ledger account over a date range
operations.description:
Retrieves account movements between `startDate` and `endDate`, optionally
including movements for one or more prior comparison periods of the same length,
and optionally filtered by account class, type, account IDs, system account code,
or tracking item.

### Filtering

- Filter by `class`, `type`, `accountIds`, and/or `systemAccountCodes`. These can be
  combined freely — when more than one is supplied, the server returns only accounts
  that match **all** of the supplied filters (an intersection, not a union).
- `type` values are matched case-sensitively, so use uppercase (for example `BANK`). Inventory
  asset accounts are reported as, and can only be filtered by, `INVENTORY`; filtering by
  their underlying account type does not match them.
- `trackingItemIds` and `unassignedToTrackingCategoryIds` can be used independently of
  the filters above to further narrow which accounts are returned.

### Comparison periods

- Supplying `comparisonPeriodCount` together with `comparisonPeriodSize` returns
  additional movements for prior date ranges of the same length, in addition to the
  movement between `startDate` and `endDate`.
- Each comparison range is calculated by moving the primary range back by
  `comparisonPeriodSize`, `comparisonPeriodCount` times. For `MONTH`, `QUARTER`, and
  `YEAR` sizes, range boundaries that fall on the last day of a month keep landing on
  the last day of the shifted month.
- `comparisonPeriodCount` and `comparisonPeriodSize` must be supplied together.
- The primary range and every comparison range must not overlap each other. A request
  whose periods would overlap is rejected with `400 Bad Request`. Ranges that share a single boundary day count as
  overlapping, which month-end adjustment can cause when shifting by `MONTH`, `QUARTER`, or
  `YEAR`.

### Bank accounts

Bank account data is only available to users with bank account view permission for the
organisation.

- If the request would include bank accounts and the user lacks this permission, it is
  rejected with `403 Forbidden`. A request is treated as including bank accounts when it
  has no account filters, filters by all five `class` values and nothing else, includes
  `BANK` in `type`, or lists a bank account in `accountIds`.
- For other requests (for example `class=ASSET`), bank accounts are silently excluded from
  the response for users without this permission, instead of the request being rejected.

### Pagination

This endpoint does not paginate — the full set of matching account movements is
returned in a single response.

### Results

Only combinations of account and date range with non-zero movement are returned; comparison
ranges are not zero-filled. The response is a flat list with no guaranteed ordering.

operations.summary: Get general ledger account transactions between two dates, with pagination and filtering
operations.description:
Retrieves transactions posted between `startDate` and `endDate` (inclusive),
optionally filtered by account IDs, class, type, or system account code, with
cursor-based pagination for large result sets.

**First call:** omit `token`. Supply `accountingBasis`, `startDate`, and
`endDate` (all required), plus any optional filters.

**Continuation calls:** supply only `token`, taken from the previous response's
`pagination.nextToken`. Do not send any other query parameters — they are
ignored if present, since the original request is captured by the token.

### Pagination

- Results are returned in pages of 200 lines.
- Use `pagination.nextToken` from the response as the `token` query parameter to fetch
  the next page. Send only the `token` query parameter on continuation requests — all
  other query parameters are
  ignored on a continuation call, since the original request's parameters are already
  captured by the token.
- The `token` value is an opaque string. Treat it as an opaque string only — do not
  parse, modify, or construct it yourself. Tokens may expire.
- When `pagination` is `null`, you've reached the last page.
- The API captures a consistent snapshot at the time of the first request (via
  `maxJournalNumber`), so transactions added while you are paginating through a
  result set won't appear partway through, and won't cause duplicates or gaps.

### Filtering

- Filter by `accountIds`, `class`, `type`, and/or `systemAccountCodes`. These can be
  combined freely — when more than one is supplied, the server returns only
  transactions for accounts that match **all** of the supplied filters (an
  intersection, not a union).
- `type` values are matched case-sensitively, so use uppercase (for example `BANK`). Inventory
  asset accounts are reported as, and can only be filtered by, `INVENTORY`; filtering by
  their underlying account type does not match them.
- Use `systemAccountCodes=NONE` to match accounts that have no system account code.
- Filters are only read from the first request in a pagination sequence — see
  Pagination above.

### Bank accounts

Bank account transactions are only available to users with bank account view permission for
the organisation.

- If the user lacks this permission and the request includes `BANK` in `type`, or lists a
  bank account in `accountIds`, it is rejected with `403 Forbidden`.
- For all other requests, including unfiltered requests, bank account transactions are
  silently excluded from the results for users without this permission.
